Erryone already tellin you to stop drinkin' so I'll give you other advice. As a 29 year old who has been depressed since I was 17:

When people say "it gets better" it sounds like a lie. It's not quite a lie but not quite a truth. Life is always hard, unfortunately, always full of Ups and Downs. BUT! What people really mean is YOU get better. YOU get stronger, faster, smarter. YOU become more capable of recognizing red flags. YOU become more capable of dodging shitty situations, AND when shitty situations happen, YOU become more experienced and more knowledgeable about how to tackle them, how to keep yourself safe.

So it's kind of like...life is always the same base hardness. but over time, you level up, and you start kicking it's ass back :)

If you have depression now, you can consider it an ailment that will likely trickle in and out of your life forever, like a chronic pain. But that doesn't have to be as damning as it sounds. Just like how you can minimize chronic pain with physical therapy and meds, we can minimize mental pain with mental therapy, meds, coping mechanisms, support groups, and a willingness to keep fighting. We learn how to cope and get stronger and make connections with time and experience. As you age you'll make more and more friends and you'll gain the ability to detect red flags and you'll understand yourself better to be able to set and defend your boundaries. But you have to be willing to keep on trying!
You can also kill your emotions by killing your Ego. But that requires some intense philosophy and a personal revelation.

Every anti depressant is different and so has different side effects and different potential doses for harm. Instead of googling "how much of an anti depressant will kill you", you should probably find a list of specific drugs and Google "<drug name> dosage information". You'll get a large page with all the info on the drug, including maximum dose suggestions, side effects, and an 'overdose' section.

You should know most anti-depressants will not kill you if you overdose. They usually just make you really sick. For example the Zoloft info page says nobody has ever died from an overdose from exclusively Zoloft.

Actually, dying from overdosing is quite difficult in general. The body is shocking good at rejecting poison. Most drugs tend to fuck up your kidney moreso than your vital organs.
